title: Weather and the earth
summary: What the sky and the ground do, and what it is called.

questions.clue: This is a long period during which far too little rain falls and the land dries out.
questions.note: It rhymes with out, not with thought, which is one of the least predictable spellings in English.

questions.clue: This is a mass of snow and ice that breaks loose and slides suddenly down a mountainside.
questions.note: From a word in the French Alps. The equivalent made of mud and rock is a landslide.

questions.clue: This is a slow-moving river of ice that carves out a valley as it travels.
questions.note: They move a few centimetres to a few metres a day. The U-shaped valleys they leave behind are the clearest evidence they were there.

questions.clue: This is the amount of water vapour held in the air, which makes a hot day feel heavy.
questions.note: High humidity stops sweat evaporating, which is why the same temperature feels far hotter in a damp climate.

questions.clue: This is a sudden violent shaking of the ground caused by movement deep below the surface.
questions.note: Tremor usually means a small one, but it answers the clue. Its strength is measured on a magnitude scale.

questions.clue: This is the gradual wearing away of rock and soil by wind, water or ice.
questions.note: Erosion carries material away. Weathering, which is a different word, breaks it down where it lies.

questions.clue: This is a violent tropical storm with spiralling winds, and it has three different names depending on the ocean it forms over.
questions.note: Exactly the same storm: hurricane in the Atlantic, typhoon in the north-west Pacific, cyclone in the Indian Ocean. All three are accepted.

questions.clue: This is the regular rise and fall of the sea, caused mainly by the pull of the moon.
questions.note: Most coasts get two high tides a day. The moon does most of the work and the sun adds to it.

questions.clue: This is the opening in the earth's surface through which molten rock is thrown out.
questions.note: The molten rock is called magma underground and lava once it reaches the air.

questions.clue: This is the layer of gases held around a planet by its gravity.
questions.note: The same word is used for the mood of a place, as in the atmosphere in the room, from the idea of something surrounding you.
